authority_basis.claim_scope: Tension modelling depends on string/pulley assumptions and is not generally equal to a hanging weight.

concepts.statement: Equal tension across ideal massless string segments is a model consequence, not a universal fact for every string/pulley system.
concepts.why_required: Tension values depend on the declared string and pulley model and on body acceleration.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may assume T=mg or equal tension across non-ideal segments without checking model assumptions.

model_conditions.condition: Any equal-tension claim is restricted to the declared ideal massless-string and ideal-pulley model.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Finite string mass, friction or pulley inertia can produce different tensions in different segments.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Segment tensions may differ and additional pulley/string dynamics are required.

model_conditions.condition: Connected bodies obey the declared geometric string constraint while the string remains taut.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The acceleration relation comes from fixed string length and routing geometry.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Bodies cannot be assigned the same or related acceleration without a valid constraint.

representations.semantic_geometry: Separate receiver-labelled FBDs are linked by the string path and an explicit acceleration constraint; tension arrows act along string segments on each receiver.
must_not_imply: equal tension survives arbitrary non-ideal string or pulley models
representations.verification_method: Substitute the solved tension into every connected body equation and verify the acceleration constraint is satisfied consistently.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare the string and pulley model before assuming any equality of tension or acceleration relation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Special ideal-string properties may be applied to a non-ideal system without justification.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Draw separate FBDs for each connected receiver and place tension arrows along the string interaction direction.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Forces on different bodies may be combined into one invalid equation.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Apply the string kinematic constraint together with each body's Newton equation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Accelerations or tension values can be solved independently even though the bodies are mechanically constrained.

required_transformations.description: Decompose the connected system into receiver-specific FBDs while preserving the common string interaction model.
Combine each body's Newton equation with the geometric string constraint to solve the coupled motion.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Tension in a moving hanging body is automatically equal to mg.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Static hanging examples give T=mg and the special result is often memorized without its zero-acceleration condition.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: For an upward-accelerating hanging mass, T-mg=ma so T is greater than mg.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the hanging-body FBD with separate upward T and downward mg arrows plus the acceleration direction.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use the body's acceleration in its Newton equation; T=mg only when the relevant acceleration is zero.
misconceptions.verification: Substitute the solved T into each body equation and verify the common acceleration constraint.

problem_families.name: Atwood-machine tension and acceleration
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the ideal-string/pulley model and draw separate FBDs before writing coupled equations.

problem_families.name: General ideal-pulley constraint problems
recognition_cues: moving pulley or multiple string segments
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the constant-string-length relation before assuming any acceleration equality.
fatal_errors: assuming all connected bodies have equal acceleration magnitude

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Treat tension as universally equal to weight without model or acceleration conditions.
